 1                                    I. INTRODUCTION

 2   Q.   PLEASE STATE YOUR NAME AND BUSINESS ADDRESS.

 3   A.   My name is Celia B. Hashlamoun. My business address is 111 East Broadway,

 4        Suite 1200, Salt Lake City, Utah, 84111.

 5   Q.   ARE YOU THE SAME CELIA B. HASHLAMOUN WHO PREVIOUSLY

 6        FILED DIRECT TESTIMONY IN THIS PROCEEDING ON BEHALF OF

 7        THE NEW MEXICO LARGE CUSTOMER GROUP (“NMLCG”)?

 8   A.   Yes, I am.

 9                           II. OVERVIEW AND CONCLUSIONS

10   Q.   WHAT         IS    THE    PURPOSE      OF    YOUR     TESTIMONY         IN   THIS

11        PROCEEDING?

12   A.   The purpose of my testimony is to support the Comprehensive Stipulation filed

13        with the New Mexico Public Regulation Commission (“Commission”) on June 22,

14        2026 (“Stipulation”). My testimony explains why the Stipulation represents a

15        reasonable resolution of the principal issues addressed in my direct testimony,

16        including SPS’s base rate revenue requirement and other ratemaking issues

17        affecting New Mexico retail customers. NMLCG witness Justin Bieber provides

18        testimony supporting the stipulated class cost of service and revenue allocation.




                                                 1
                                           Case No. 25-00079-UT
                              Stipulation Testimony of Celia B. Hashlamoun

 1   Q.      WHAT        IS     THE     PRIMARY          RECOMMENDATION                 OF     YOUR

 2           TESTIMONY?

 3   A.      For the reasons explained in my testimony below, together with the testimony of

 4           NMLCG witness Justin Bieber, NMLCG supports the Stipulation as being in the

 5           public interest and recommends that the Commission approve the Stipulation in its

 6           entirety.

 7   Q.      PLEASE PROVIDE AN OVERVIEW OF THE STIPULATION.

 8   A.      The Signatories1 to the Stipulation agree that SPS should be authorized to

 9           implement an increase in New Mexico retail base rate revenues of $90,000,000,

10           effective December 1, 2026. 2 The Stipulation identifies a return on equity (“ROE”)

11           of 9.5% and several cost-of-service components, including capital structure, SPS’s

12           working capital balance and depreciation rates.3

13           Additionally, the Stipulation provides for:

14               •   A modification to the 12-coincident peak production (“12-CP PROD”)

15                   jurisdictional allocator to exclude the load served by the directly assigned

16                   Cunningham Battery Energy Storage System (“BESS”) capacity resource,




     1
        The Signatories are: SPS, the New Mexico Department of Justice (“NMDOJ”), NMLCG, Occidental
     Permian Ltd. (“OPL”), Louisiana Energy Services L.L.C. (“LES”), Federal Executive Agencies (“FEA”),
     Targa Resources Corp. (“Targa”), Walmart Inc. (“Walmart”), Coalition for Clean Affordable Energy
     (“CCAE”), and Prosperity Works. Commission Staff does not oppose parts of the Stipulation.
     2
       Comprehensive Stipulation, p.3 (Jun. 22, 2026) (“Stipulation”).
     3
       Id. at pp. 3-5.

 1                    thereby reflecting New Mexico retail customers’ reduced reliance on other

 2                    shared system production resources;4

 3               •    Temporary withdrawal of SPS’s proposal to recover six BESS Long Term

 4                    Purchased Power Agreements (“LTPPA”) costs through its Fuel Purchased

 5                    Power Cost Adjustment Clause (“FPPCAC”);5

 6               •    Withdrawal of SPS’s proposal to recover Southwest Power Pool (“SPP”)

 7                    deficiency payments through its FPPCAC;6

 8               •    Withdrawal of SPS’s proposal to implement both a property tax and excess

 9                    liability insurance tracker;7

10               •    A return on the production tax credit (“PTC”) deferred tax assets (“DTA”)

11                    associated with certain SPS solar projects8 equal to SPS’s cost of debt;9 and

12               •    SPS’s agreement not to retain off-system sales margins from the

13                    Cunningham BESS and Plant X Solar Projects.10

14                    Other than the cost-of-service components identified in the Stipulation, the

15           stipulated base rate revenue increase is not tied to any specific calculation or

16           approval or disapproval of any other issue raised in this case.11

 1               The Signatories arrived at the stipulated base rate revenue increase through

 2        a compromise of the various issues raised in this case without specifically accepting

 3        or rejecting any ratemaking issue or principle other than those specified in the

 4        Stipulation.

 5              III. NMLCG’S SUPPORT FOR THE STIPULATION

 6   Q.   PLEASE EXPLAIN WHY THE NMLCG SUPPORTS THE STIPULATED

 7        BASE RATE REVENUE INCREASE.

 8   A.   In its direct case, SPS requested a base rate increase of $175.4 million. SPS

 9        subsequently filed revisions that reduced the revenue requirement by

10        approximately $3.1 million. NMLCG recommended a base rate increase of $28.2

11        million based on the adjustments presented in my direct testimony and the

12        testimony of Mr. David Garrett.

13               Although the stipulated revenue requirement of $90 million is greater than

14        that proposed by the NMLCG in testimony, it is substantially below SPS’s original

15        request and reflects a negotiated compromise among the Signatories. Importantly,

16        SPS’s request also included proposals that could have increased customer costs or

17        shifted additional risk to customers beyond the base revenue increase itself,

18        including proposed tracker mechanisms, FPPCAC recovery of certain non-fuel

19        costs, and retention of off-system sales margins related to Cunningham BESS and

20        Plant X Solar Projects.




                                                4
                                     Case No. 25-00079-UT
                        Stipulation Testimony of Celia B. Hashlamoun

 1               The Stipulation resolves these issues in a manner that provides meaningful

 2        customer protections. For that reason, NMLCG does not evaluate the $90 million

 3        base rate increase in isolation. When considered together with the other terms of

 4        the Stipulation, NMLCG believes the stipulated base rate increase represents a

 5        reasonable compromise and supports approval of the Stipulation as a whole.

 6   Q.   WHAT OTHER RATEMAKING TERMS OF THE STIPULATION

 7        SUPPORT NMLCG’S RECOMMENDATION?

 8   A.   In addition to the stipulated base rate revenue increase, NMLCG’s recommendation

 9        is supported by several other ratemaking provisions in the Stipulation, including

10        the treatment of the Cunningham BESS, the withdrawal or temporary withdrawal

11        of certain FPPCAC recovery proposals, the limitation of SPS’s return on certain

12        PTC-related deferred tax asset balances, the withdrawal of proposed tracker

13        mechanisms, and SPS’s agreement not to retain certain off-system sales margins. I

14        discuss these provisions below.

15   Q.   PLEASE EXPLAIN HOW THE STIPULATION ADDRESSES THE

16        NMLCG’S CONCERNS REGARDING THE DIRECT ASSIGNMENT OF

17        CUNNINGHAM BESS COSTS AND BENEFITS.

18   A.   In my direct testimony, I recommended that if the Commission were to approve

19        SPS’s proposal to directly assign the Cunningham BESS to New Mexico retail

20        customers, the Company should also be required to modify its 12-CP PROD

21        jurisdictional allocator to reflect New Mexico’s customers’ reduced reliance on the



                                               5
                                          Case No. 25-00079-UT
                             Stipulation Testimony of Celia B. Hashlamoun

 1           other shared system capacity resources.12 I concluded that failing to make such an

 2           adjustment would result in New Mexico’s retail customers paying twice for the

 3           same capacity: first, through the direct assignment of the Cunningham BESS

 4           resource and again through an unadjusted share of the remaining shared system

 5           capacity resources.13

 6                    The Stipulation adopts this NMLCG recommendation by providing for a

 7           specific calculation that modifies the 12-CP PROD allocator for the directly

 8           assigned resource.       The Stipulation also establishes a stakeholder process to

 9           evaluate the treatment of directly assigned resources and the jurisdictional

10           allocation of divergent state resource portfolios for future proceedings prior to SPS

11           filing its next base rate case. This represents a reasonable resolution of this issue.

12   Q.      PLEASE EXPLAIN HOW THE STIPULATION ADDRESSES THE

13           NMLCG’S CONCERNS REGARDING RECOVERY OF BESS LTPPA

14           COSTS AND DEFICIENCY PAYMENTS.

15   A.      In my direct testimony, I opposed SPS’s proposal to recover the BESS LTPPA

16           capacity costs,14 and also opposed SPS’s proposal to recover potential SPP

17           deficiency payments from customers through the FPPCAC.15 I concluded that this

        Direct Testimony and Attachments of Celia B. Hashlamoun, pp. 18-19 (May 1, 2026).

                                                       6
                                            Case No. 25-00079-UT
                               Stipulation Testimony of Celia B. Hashlamoun

 1               latter proposal is inconsistent with the intended purposes of the FPPCAC and could

 2               improperly shift costs and risks to customers.16

 3                        The Stipulation temporarily withdraws SPS’s proposal to recover BESS

 4               LTPPA costs through the FPPCAC and withdraws SPS’s proposal to recover SPP

 5               deficiency payments through the FPPCAC. These provisions reasonably address

 6               the concerns raised in my direct testimony and preserve the FPPCAC as a

 7               mechanism for recovery of appropriate variable fuel and purchase power costs

 8               rather than fixed contractual costs or other non-fuel expenses.

 9   Q.          ARE THERE OTHER ASPECTS OF THE STIPULATION THAT

10               SUPPORT THE NMLCG’S RECOMENDATION?

11   A.          Yes. In my direct testimony, I opposed SPS’s proposal to earn its full authorized

12               rate of return on PTC-related DTA balances associated with SPS’s Solar Projects

13               because SPS did not demonstrate that those balances warrant recovery at its full

14               authorized return.17

15                        The Stipulation limits SPS’s return on the applicable PTC-related DTA

16               balances to its cost of debt.     This represents a reasonable compromise and

17               appropriately recognizes the lower risk these balances have relative to traditional

18               utility investments.




     16
          Id. at pp. 40-41.
     17
          Id. at pp. 36-38.




                                                      7
                                              Case No. 25-00079-UT
                                 Stipulation Testimony of Celia B. Hashlamoun

 1                        The Stipulation also withdraws SPS’s proposed property tax and excess

 2               liability insurance trackers. As explained in my direct testimony, NMLCG opposed

 3               these proposals because they would result in single-issue ratemaking and could

 4               have shifted additional cost risk to customers outside of a traditional base rate

 5               proceeding.18    Their withdrawal preserves Commission review of these costs

 6               through future base rate cases and avoids piecemeal recovery mechanisms.

 7                        Lastly, the Stipulation provides that SPS will not retain off-system sales

 8               margins for the Cunningham BESS and Plant X Solar Projects. This provision

 9               appropriately protects customer interests and avoids allocating a portion of those

10               margins to shareholders.

11   Q.          DOES THIS CONCLUDE YOUR DIRECT TESTIMONY?

12   A.          Yes, it does.
